newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-GALFIONE OUTSHINES HAMALAINEN IN DECATHLON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GALFIONE OUTSHINES HAMALAINEN IN DECATHLON.

text.p: Eduard Hamalainen of Belarus defeated Olympic bronze medallist Tomas Dvorak to win a decathlon on Sunday.
Hamalainen notched 8,478 points, way below his personal best of 8,735 points, to score a narrow victory over Czech pair Dvorak (8,456) and Robert Zmelik (8,425).
Olympic champion Dan O'Brien of the U.S. did not contest the two-day event.

Frenchman Jean Galfione, the Olympic pole vault champion, achieved the best-ever decathlon pole vault height of 5.75 metres, surpassing the 5.70 cleared by American Tim Bright at the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Galfione figured nowhere in the final classification, compiling 7,206 points which left him more than 1,200 behind the top three. But his vault earned him wild applause from the home crowd.

In the heptathlon, Hamalainen's compatriot Natalya Sazanovich dropped from first to fourth overall when she cracked in the concluding 800 metres. Lithuania's Remigija Nazarovienne won the event with 6,451 points.
